sentences.text: Magnamanus was a large herbivorous dinosaur belonging to the iguanodontians, a group of ornithopods that measured between 9 and 10 meters in length and weighed approximately 3 metric tons.
The genus name Magnamanus combines the Latin words for 'large' and 'hand' to reference the animal's unusually wide wrists, which spanned 70% of the total hand length.
Its skeleton, discovered between 2000 and 2004, stands as one of the most complete dinosaur remains from the Lower Cretaceous of Spain.
Named and described in 2016 by Carolina Fuentes Vidarte and colleagues, the species Magnamanus soriaensis is known from a single fossil occurrence found in the Golmayo Formation.
This animal belongs to the bird-hipped dinosaurs, Ornithischia, and is classified within the suborder Styracosterna, occupying a rather basal position in the group Ankylopollexia.
Magnamanus soriaensis lived approximately 130 million years ago during the Barremian stage, specifically between 132.6 and 121.4 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
